INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the key question of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. How far is the market?
   B. How should we respond to instructions?
   C. Who is the tallest pupil?
   D. What is the price of food?

2. Singular means (1 mark)
   A. half
   B. one
   C. many
   D. none

3. What is a good way to give feedback to a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Say they are bad
   B. Laugh at mistakes
   C. Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   D. Say nothing

4. What should you leave between two words? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. No space
   C. A whole line
   D. A finger space

5. How should you sit when you write? (1 mark)
   A. Lying on the desk
   B. With your back turned
   C. Straight, with your book in front of you
   D. Standing on the chair

6. A newsreader on the radio should speak (1 mark)
   A. with no pauses
   B. clearly and at a steady pace
   C. in a whisper
   D. very fast

7. What does a comma tell a reader? (1 mark)
   A. To shout
   B. To turn the page
   C. To stop completely
   D. To take a short pause

8. What does a full stop show? (1 mark)
   A. A question
   B. The end of a statement
   C. A list of items
   D. A sudden feeling

9. Which sentence ends correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot,
   B. The sun is hot:
   C. The sun is hot.
   D. The sun is hot?

10. In the story of Otieno, what caused his burn? (1 mark)
   A. He ate hot food
   B. He played with a dog
   C. He touched the handle of the hot pot
   D. He fell from a tree

11. Why do we listen to oral texts about safety? (1 mark)
   A. To sleep
   B. To count the words
   C. To learn how to stay safe
   D. To waste time

12. What can you use to practise reordering sentences? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. A hammer
   C. A bucket
   D. Cut strips and arrange them

13. A good storyteller (1 mark)
   A. whispers all the time
   B. practises and speaks clearly
   C. forgets the ending
   D. reads without looking

14. What can wall charts of similes and metaphors help with? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking
   B. Sleeping
   C. Gallery walks and learning from each other
   D. Running

15. What does the Kiswahili proverb Kidole kimoja hakivunji chawa teach? (1 mark)
   A. Lice are dangerous
   B. Never use your hands
   C. One finger is very strong
   D. We need to work together

16. A saying such as It is raining cats and dogs means (1 mark)
   A. it is raining very heavily
   B. dogs and cats are lost
   C. the weather is cold
   D. animals are falling

17. Which is a character in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The rainy season
   B. A shady tree
   C. The end
   D. A girl called Neema

18. A good ending to an imaginative story usually (1 mark)
   A. has no full stops
   B. starts a new problem always
   C. repeats the title
   D. solves the problem or shows the lesson

19. In front of means (1 mark)
   A. under it
   B. behind it
   C. before something and facing it
   D. inside it

20. Which is a poem's mood if it is joyful? (1 mark)
   A. Angry
   B. Sleepy
   C. Happy
   D. Sad

21. Which tense is used to tell a story about what happened? (1 mark)
   A. Only the future
   B. Only questions
   C. No tense
   D. The past tense

22. How should peer feedback be given? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   C. Rudely
   D. Loudly

23. Why should you ask permission before using someone's phone? (1 mark)
   A. It is illegal to touch phones
   B. It is a game
   C. It belongs to them and needs care
   D. Phones never break

24. Which is a difference between an advert and a news item? (1 mark)
   A. They are exactly the same
   B. An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   C. News is always a poem
   D. Adverts report elections only

25. What should a newsreader do? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Skip words
   C. Speak clearly at a steady pace
   D. Mumble

26. What is the purpose of the instructions on a form? (1 mark)
   A. To make it hard
   B. To tell you how to fill it in
   C. To hide the title
   D. To use up space

27. What is polite when you want to speak in a discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Snatch the talking stick
   B. Shout
   C. Raise your hand or signal
   D. Stand on a chair

28. Why do we read poems? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To hide feelings
   C. To enjoy language and learn lessons
   D. To stop reading

29. Which is the first step in understanding a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Tear it
   B. Copy it
   C. Ignore it
   D. Read the title and the poem aloud

30. Which is a signal word for the second step? (1 mark)
   A. Next
   B. Yesterday
   C. Never
   D. Finally

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why sequencing ideas is important in writing. (3 marks)

32. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

33. Read: Millet porridge is a warm drink made by mixing millet flour with water and boiling it. What is it made from and how is it cooked? (3 marks)

34. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

35. Write an advert of four sentences for hand-made baskets. Include a headline, two adjectives, a price and where to buy. (5 marks)

36. List three note points from a passage about a kite on a free day. (3 marks)

37. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

38. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)

39. Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper. (3 marks)

40. Divide into subject and predicate: My brother saves coins. (2 marks)

41. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

42. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)

43. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)

44. What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful? (2 marks)

45. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — How should we respond to instructions?
   The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

2. B — one
   A singular noun names one person, animal, place or thing.

3. C — Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

4. D — A finger space
   A finger width keeps words clear.

5. C — Straight, with your book in front of you
   Good posture helps neat writing.

6. B — clearly and at a steady pace
   News should be clear and easy to follow.

7. D — To take a short pause
   Commas show short pauses.

8. B — The end of a statement
   A full stop ends a statement.

9. C — The sun is hot.
   A statement ends with a full stop.

10. C — He touched the handle of the hot pot
   He moved closer and touched the handle, and the pot tipped.

11. C — To learn how to stay safe
   Safety texts teach what to do and what to avoid.

12. D — Cut strips and arrange them
   Strips of sentences can be moved into order.

13. B — practises and speaks clearly
   Practice and clarity make a good teller.

14. C — Gallery walks and learning from each other
   Charts display the sayings for review.

15. D — We need to work together
   One finger cannot crush a louse, so cooperation is needed.

16. A — it is raining very heavily
   It is an expression for heavy rain.

17. D — A girl called Neema
   Characters are the people or animals.

18. D — solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

19. C — before something and facing it
   In front of shows the position ahead of something.

20. C — Happy
   A joyful poem has a happy mood.

21. D — The past tense
   Stories about past events use the past.

22. B — Kindly, with one good point and one suggestion
   Kind feedback helps writers.

23. C — It belongs to them and needs care
   Respecting others' property is polite.

24. B — An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   Their purposes differ.

25. C — Speak clearly at a steady pace
   Clear speech helps listeners.

26. B — To tell you how to fill it in
   Instructions guide the person filling it.

27. C — Raise your hand or signal
   Signal politely.

28. C — To enjoy language and learn lessons
   Poems entertain and teach.

29. D — Read the title and the poem aloud
   Reading aloud comes first.

30. A — Next
   Next shows the following step.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader follow the ideas, avoids confusion and makes writing logical.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each valid point.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is made from millet flour and water and it is cooked by boiling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for millet flour, one for water, one for boiling.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any advert with a headline, two adjectives, a price and a place, for example: Strong Baskets for Sale. Our baskets are big and colourful. Only 300 shillings each. Buy at the market gate.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the four required features and one mark for clear sentences.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Children go to the field, fly a paper kite, string breaks, grandfather mends the kite (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each short correct note.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule, up to three.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Subject: My brother. Predicate: saves coins.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.
